Subject: Deployment path clarification: isolation expectations and next steps

Hi Katie —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap and a set of clarifying questions so we can prepare the right technical deep-dive: 

Recap of what I heard
- Primary concern: strict data isolation for regulated customer data (transactional PII and logs).
- Goal is to ensure data and audit logs remain within FinX control and to understand whether model weights or inference execution in vendor-managed infra is acceptable.

High-level deployment options (summary):
- Hosted API: fastest to go-live but runs in Redwood-hosted multi-tenant environment — not a fit if you require vendor-zero persistence or customer-only key control.
- Dedicated capacity: customer-dedicated GPU pool managed by Redwood. Can be configured with VPC peering or private network connectivity and customer-managed KMS for at-rest encryption. Model runtime still occurs on Redwood-managed hardware.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full customer-controlled deployment (VPC or on-prem package) — model weights and runtime live in your environment; recommended when regulators disallow any vendor-managed persistence or access.

Questions for you before the technical call
1) Is the non-negotiable requirement that model weights and any cached inference artifacts must never be stored in Redwood-managed hardware?
2) Do you require logs and telemetry to be pushed into an AWS account owned by FinX (S3/CloudWatch) as a hard requirement?
3) Any particular compliance references (e.g., specific regulator guidance or audit language) we should map to?

Next steps
- If you confirm (1) or (2) above, we’ll prep two tracks for the deep-dive: Dedicated with VPC-connect design and Private on-prem/VPC deployment design.
- I’ve attached a short security one-pager and a deployment requirements template to collect the network/security details we’ll need.
- Proposed time for the technical meet: Thurs 2026-08-05 09:00 PT — please confirm.

Thanks,

Sergio —

Thanks for the summary. A few clarifications: 
- Our compliance and internal audit teams require that customer data (including PII and transactional logs) never persist in a vendor-managed bucket or storage for more than transient memory (i.e., must be exported to our S3/GCS and then purged on our schedule).
- We also have a strong preference for customer-managed encryption keys. If Redwood can support a model where logs/metrics are streamed into an FinX AWS account and keys are customer-managed, that helps a lot.
- On model weights: our initial posture is that model weights used for inference may remain on vendor-managed hardware only if we have legal and technical assurances (audit logs, key separation, and contractual controls). If those cannot be met, we'll need Private deployment.

I think your proposed approach (two-track prep) makes sense. Please include any examples of customers who used Dedicated with VPC-connect + customer KMS, and any differences we should expect versus a Private on-prem install. Also include an estimate range for committed monthly cost for Dedicated (ballpark GPUs/month) — procurement will need that for early review. Our procurement contact is Samuel Jones (samuel.jones@finxbank.com).

-Katie
Katie Winters

Hi Katie —

Thanks for the clear constraints; I wanted to add technical color so you can see where Dedicated vs Private typically diverge in practice: 

Dedicated capacity (what we call Redwood Dedicated)
- Hardware: dedicated GPU nodes logically isolated to your tenant. The infrastructure (hosts, device drivers, hypervisor/containers) is still managed by Redwood.
- Networking: supports VPC peering or private peering (transit), and we can arrange private endpoints so control plane traffic is limited.
- Key management: supports customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) for at-rest encryption of persisted artifacts we control; logs and telemetry can be exported to your AWS account via secure sinks.
- Model weights: typically loaded onto Redwood-managed GPUs at runtime; ephemeral caches can be configured to minimize persistence. We can document cache lifetimes and purge behavior and provide audit hooks.
- Tradeoffs: much faster provisioning and lower ops burden for FinX; still requires contractual and technical controls if your policy forbids vendor-hosted weights.

Private deployment (VPC-hosted or on-prem package)
- Hardware and runtime live in your environment (either in your VPC where you control instances or fully on-prem air-gapped appliances).
- You retain full control of keys, storage, and model artifacts. Redwood provides a private control plane or an appliance package depending on the engagement.
- Tradeoffs: highest isolation and easiest to satisfy conservative auditors, but longer lead times and additional SW/HW integration work.

Options and asks from FinX for next step prep
1) Confirm whether model weights absolutely cannot be present on vendor-managed hardware even transiently (yes/no).
2) Provide a sample network CIDR and whether you prefer VPC peering or an S3-forwarding-only model for logs.
3) Compliance pack request: we’ll send our SOC2 summary and prior deployment diagrams. Can you share the specific control numbers your auditors will validate?

I’ve attached our SOC2_summary.pdf and a VPC connect reference diagram (vpc_connect_arch.png). If it helps, we can share anonymized case notes of customers who adopted Dedicated with customer KMS and VPC export for logs.

Happy to join the technical deep-dive and walk through a proposed architecture.

Best,
